items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I mean I’ve sat in on Ornette’s sessions. Ornette is a meticulous planner.

ctx.x: Well I think that Coltrane was going for some — I don’t think he ever made — I don’t know. It strikes me that he had an ideal in mind that no realization was ever going to

reach, he was never going to attain. I think Coltrane had some very high standards. And the marvelous thing about Coltrane is that he tried to — he went for them. And just by going for them, however short he falls of actually having us ascend, you know, he gives us a platform so that we can begin to see what “Ascension” might really be. He gives us some sort of lift and launch. It’s not all experimentation on those records either. I mean “Free Jazz,” they released a twenty minute version that Ornette did as a…
And no one’s going to enjoy it either.
